facts.text: On 2007-07-10, EU finance ministers agreed to back Dominique Strauss-Kahn as the next managing director of the IMF, while Britain refused to abide by the decision.
On 2008-10-18, the IMF began an inquiry into whether Dominique Strauss-Kahn abused his position through a sexual relationship with a subordinate, a charge he denied.

On 2011-05-14, Dominique Strauss-Kahn, head of the IMF, was arrested and charged with sexually assaulting and attempting to rape a maid in a New York hotel; he resigned as managing director on 2011-05-18.

On 2011-08-23, a New York judge dismissed the criminal sexual assault charges against Dominique Strauss-Kahn after prosecutors said they could not prove the case beyond a reasonable doubt due to credibility issues with his accuser.

On 2011-11-11, Dominique Strauss-Kahn demanded to be interviewed by investigative judges in the Lille Hotel Carlton prostitution-ring case, denouncing a "media lynching" after his name was linked to the investigation.

On 2012-03-26, a French judge charged former IMF head Dominique Strauss-Kahn over alleged links with a prostitution ring, placing him under formal investigation for "complicity in aggravated and organised prostitution" and "misuse of company assets."

On 2012-10-02, French prosecutors dropped a preliminary inquiry into whether Dominique Strauss-Kahn could face rape charges over the alleged group rape of a Belgian sex worker, though he remained under formal investigation over alleged complicity in a pimping operation.
On 2012-12-10, Dominique Strauss-Kahn settled a civil sexual assault lawsuit with hotel maid Nafissatou Diallo for a confidential sum, ending her New York court battle against him.

facts.text: On 2007-07-10, EU finance ministers agreed to back Dominique Strauss-Kahn as the next managing director of the IMF, while Britain refused to abide by the decision.
On 2008-10-18, the IMF began an inquiry into whether Dominique Strauss-Kahn abused his position through a sexual relationship with a subordinate, a charge he denied.

On 2011-05-14, Dominique Strauss-Kahn, head of the IMF, was arrested and charged with sexually assaulting and attempting to rape a maid in a New York hotel; he resigned as managing director on 2011-05-18.

On 2011-07-01, Dominique Strauss-Kahn was freed from house arrest and had his bail dropped after prosecutors discovered his accuser had lied about a previous rape claim and other key elements of her account.

On 2011-08-23, a New York judge dismissed the criminal sexual assault charges against Dominique Strauss-Kahn after prosecutors said they could not prove the case beyond a reasonable doubt due to credibility issues with his accuser.

On 2012-03-26, a French judge charged former IMF head Dominique Strauss-Kahn over alleged links with a prostitution ring, placing him under formal investigation for "complicity in aggravated and organised prostitution" and "misuse of company assets."
On 2012-12-10, Dominique Strauss-Kahn settled a civil sexual assault lawsuit with hotel maid Nafissatou Diallo for a confidential sum, ending her New York court battle against him.
On 2015-02-11, in court during his Lille trial on aggravated pimping charges, a second woman, Jade, testified that Dominique Strauss-Kahn subjected her to a sex act against her will.

facts.text: On 2007-07-10, EU finance ministers agreed to back Dominique Strauss-Kahn as the next managing director of the IMF, while Britain refused to abide by the decision.
On 2008-10-18, the IMF began an inquiry into whether Dominique Strauss-Kahn abused his position through a sexual relationship with a subordinate, a charge he denied.

On 2011-05-14, Dominique Strauss-Kahn, head of the IMF, was arrested and charged with sexually assaulting and attempting to rape a maid in a New York hotel; he resigned as managing director on 2011-05-18.
On 2011-05-16, Dominique Strauss-Kahn faced allegations of attempted rape and sexual assault, including a planned police complaint by Tristane Banon, which he denied.

On 2011-07-01, Dominique Strauss-Kahn was freed from house arrest and had his bail dropped after prosecutors discovered his accuser had lied about a previous rape claim and other key elements of her account.

On 2011-08-23, a New York judge dismissed the criminal sexual assault charges against Dominique Strauss-Kahn after prosecutors said they could not prove the case beyond a reasonable doubt due to credibility issues with his accuser.

On 2012-03-26, a French judge charged former IMF head Dominique Strauss-Kahn over alleged links with a prostitution ring, placing him under formal investigation for "complicity in aggravated and organised prostitution" and "misuse of company assets."

On 2015-02-12, Dominique Strauss-Kahn told a French court he rented a luxury Paris flat under an acquaintance's name because he was married and wanted a discreet place to meet women for group sex, as he stands trial on charges of aggravated pimping, which he denies.

Dominique Strauss-Kahn was acquitted on charges of aggravated pimping, though public opinion in France continues to condemn him.
Warner Bros is developing a film titled The Libertine, a comedic dramatisation based on the Dominique Strauss-Kahn sexual assault scandal, with no casting or director yet announced.
Johnny Depp and Marion Cotillard are set to star in a Dominique Strauss-Kahn-inspired drama titled The Libertine for director Brett Ratner.
